title: Unauthorized Account Takeover During Enrollment
description: An attacker could impersonate the Homeowner (EE1) to register and enroll cameras/sensors on the Home Hub (P1), gaining unauthorized control over the security system.
assumptions: Attacker has access to Homeowner credentials or can exploit weak authentication mechanisms during the enrollment process.

title: Privacy Data Disclosure During Account Registration
description: Homeowner's personal information (name, address, contact details) could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties during the account registration process on the Home Hub.
assumptions: The Home Hub or backend system may have inadequate access controls or logging vulnerabilities that expose sensitive enrollment data.

title: Homeowner Identification from Device Enrollment Data
description: The Homeowner's identity could be inferred or directly identified from the device enrollment records stored on the Home Hub, potentially enabling profiling or tracking.
assumptions: Enrollment data contains personally identifiable information that could be accessed or correlated with other data sources.

title: Linkability of Homeowner to Device Usage Patterns
description: The Homeowner's identity could be linked to their device usage patterns and camera/sensor data, enabling behavioral profiling and potential surveillance.
assumptions: The system logs and stores detailed usage metadata that could be correlated with the Homeowner's identity.

title: Guest Linkability via Access Code Entry
description: An observer at the front door could observe the guest entering an access code, potentially linking this guest to the household and other activities. The act of entering a code at a specific time/location could be correlated with other data flows or system events.
assumptions: Observer has line-of-sight to the entry point and can observe code entry behavior
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable fit for linkability at the source position

title: Guest Identifiability from Access Code
description: The temporary access code entry could reveal the guest's identity to observers or through system logging. If codes are personalized or if entry logs are accessible, the guest could be identified from this interaction.
assumptions: Access codes may be personalized or entry is logged in a way that reveals identity
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a standard node for identifiability at source position

title: Excessive Data Collection on Access Code Entry
description: The Home Hub process may collect more data than necessary from the guest's access code entry (e.g., timestamp, device info, entry method) beyond what's needed for door unlocking, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: System logs or stores additional metadata beyond the access code itself
uncertainty_note: Dd.1.1 is a standard node for data minimization at process position

title: Unauthorized Access via Code Sharing or Theft
description: The temporary access code could be shared, observed, or stolen by unauthorized parties, allowing them to gain access to the home. This represents a usurpation of the legitimate guest's access rights.
assumptions: Access codes can be observed, shared, or intercepted by unauthorized parties
uncertainty_note: U.1.1 is a standard node for usurpation at process position

title: Linkability of motion/sensor events
description: Motion, door, and sensor events written to the local event log could be linked together to reconstruct detailed patterns of household activity, revealing occupancy schedules, routines, and presence patterns.
assumptions: Events are timestamped and contain sufficient detail to correlate across different sensor types.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is inferred from context; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Identification of household occupants
description: Motion and door events could be used to identify who is present at home, when they arrive/leave, and their movement patterns within the house.
assumptions: Event data contains enough detail (e.g., location, timing) to infer occupant presence.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is inferred from context; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of event log
description: The local event log (DS1) could be accessed by unauthorized parties, potentially through physical access, network compromise, or insecure storage, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: The local event log is not adequately protected from unauthorized access.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 is inferred from context; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Tampering with event log data
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could modify, delete, or inject false events, compromising the integrity of the security monitoring system.
assumptions: The event log is not protected against unauthorized modification.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from context; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Linkability of video clips to other data sources
description: Cloud video storage may allow linking of camera clips to other user data, profiles, or surveillance systems, enabling correlation of activities across different contexts.
assumptions: Cloud storage system may have access to or integration with other data sources; metadata may be retained.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is a reasonable fit for linkability at DataStore position

title: Identifiability of individuals in video footage
description: Stored camera clips inherently contain identifiable information about people in the home, enabling recognition and tracking of individuals without their consent.
assumptions: Video footage captures recognizable human faces or activities; no anonymization is applied.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a standard node for identifiability at DataStore

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored video clips
description: Cloud video storage may be accessible to unauthorized parties through security breaches, insider threats, or improper access controls, leading to privacy violations.
assumptions: Cloud storage has access controls that may be compromised; third-party cloud providers may have access to data.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 is appropriate for disclosure at DataStore position

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations for video surveillance
description: Storage of camera footage may violate GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations regarding video surveillance, data retention, and user consent requirements.
assumptions: Applicable privacy laws require explicit consent, limited retention, and specific handling of surveillance data.
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 is a reasonable node for regulatory compliance at DataStore

title: Excessive motion data disclosure to backend
description: Home Hub (P1) forwards real-time motion alert data to Mobile App Backend (P2). This transfer may disclose personal data about occupancy patterns, daily routines, or presence in the home beyond what is strictly necessary for the alert function.
assumptions: Motion data contains personal information about household presence and activities; the backend may retain or further process this data.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.4 from context [5] as it addresses excessive exposure to known parties (the backend system). The exact scope of personal data in motion alerts is inferred from typical smart home data characteristics.

title: Linkability of motion detection notifications to homeowner profile
description: The motion-detected notification could be linked to other data about the homeowner's property, behavior patterns, or security events, potentially revealing sensitive information about their habits or presence at the property.
assumptions: The notification contains or can be correlated with other data about the homeowner or property.

title: Unauthorized interception of motion notification
description: The notification transmitted from the mobile app backend to the homeowner's phone could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the homeowner's property location and activity patterns.
assumptions: The communication channel is not fully secured or encryption is insufficient.

title: Usurpation of homeowner identity for notification access
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the homeowner to receive motion detection notifications, gaining awareness of property activity without authorization.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms for notification delivery are not sufficiently robust.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud analytics vendor may be linkable with other data sources (e.g., user profiles, device identifiers) to re-identify individuals or create detailed user profiles across systems.
assumptions: Analytics data contains residual identifying information or can be correlated with other datasets
uncertainty_note: Context [3] confirms Process→ExternalEntity flow supports L threat at S/fl/D positions

title: Unauthorized Disclosure to External Vendor
description: Mobile app backend shares aggregated analytics with external cloud analytics vendor (EE3), creating risk of data disclosure to unauthorized parties if vendor security controls are inadequate or if data is accessed by unauthorized personnel within the vendor organization.
assumptions: External vendor may have insufficient security controls or access controls
uncertainty_note: Context [3] confirms Process→ExternalEntity flow supports D threat at S/fl/D positions

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation in Data Transfer
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with external cloud analytics vendor may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, data minimization, or cross-border transfer requirements are not met.
assumptions: Data transfer may not comply with applicable privacy regulations
uncertainty_note: Context [3] confirms Process→ExternalEntity flow supports Nc threat at S/fl/D positions

title: Identifiability of video content
description: Video clips stored in the cloud contain identifiable information about the homeowner and potentially other individuals. When retrieved by the mobile app backend, this data can be used to identify specific persons, creating privacy risks.
assumptions: Video content contains recognizable faces or identifiable activities

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data
description: The mobile app backend may disclose video data to unauthorized parties through insecure transmission, improper access controls, or data leakage during processing.
assumptions: Inadequate access controls or encryption during data transmission

title: Usurpation of homeowner identity
description: An attacker could impersonate the homeowner to access and retrieve video clips from the cloud storage, potentially viewing private footage they should not see.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms are weak or compromised

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video data may be retained longer than necessary for the intended playback purpose, violating data minimization and storage limitation principles.
assumptions: No clear retention policy or automatic deletion mechanism
uncertainty_note: Context [4] provides Nc.1.1.4 node for storage limitation, but specific retention policies for this flow are not documented
